data.narrative: Completed Module 01 Setup & Clean Code: chose single-app layout, built a FastAPI service with a GET /health endpoint and fail-fast PORT validation, and passed the failure-first drill. Diagnosed and fixed an injected APP_PORT-vs-PORT env mismatch by reading the startup error and restoring the config field contract. Demonstrated solid production thinking and hypothesis-driven debugging throughout.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose single-app over monorepo and justified with concrete constraints (single container deploy, YAGNI, worker can be an entry point later) rather than convenience.
dimension_scores.evidence: Decision reasoning: 'Single-app repo keeps setup fast and deploy simple (one folder, one container)... monorepo tooling is premature complexity we do not need yet.'

dimension_scores.observation: Formed a hypothesis from the ValidationError, verified against .env, fixed the field, then ran a regression check (restart + curl health) before closing.
dimension_scores.evidence: Server would not start with 'app_port Field required'; diagnosed env-name mismatch and confirmed fix with curl /health returning {ok:true}.

dimension_scores.observation: Kept secrets out of git via .env.example placeholders plus .gitignore, and flagged that redirect stays public while admin routes must be protected and rate-limited.
dimension_scores.evidence: Created .gitignore excluding .env; .env.example uses placeholder values; verified discussion of public-vs-protected route split.

dimension_scores.observation: Applied fail-fast config validation with boundary checks and connected it to the real APP_PORT/PORT production incident; named remaining risk (no persistence/auth/tests).
dimension_scores.evidence: PORT=abc, 0, 70000 all rejected before startup with clear errors; noted the app cannot safely serve real traffic yet.

dimension_scores.observation: Explained env validation, layout tradeoffs, and the root cause in plain language with the decision-evidence-tradeoff-verification pattern.
dimension_scores.evidence: Answer strengthening used in VERIFY and REFLECT: short, specific, plain-language answers with reproducible proof.

strengths: Applied the failure-first drill live: invalid PORT values (blank, non-number, boundary 0 and 70000) all failed fast before the server started.
Closed the debugging loop with a regression check: restart + curl /health returned {ok:true} after the fix.
Root-caused the injected bug from the error message (app_port missing) and connected it to the CONTEXT incident (APP_PORT vs PORT).
growth_areas: Could strengthen tradeoff depth by quantifying costs (e.g., estimated time saved by single-app vs monorepo setup overhead).
data.recommendation: Before Module 02, install Docker Desktop so local Postgres can run for the database module, and note the connection URL in .env.

public_evidence.student_action: Built a FastAPI service with fail-fast PORT validation and a GET /health endpoint, chose single-app layout, and verified via the failure-first drill.
public_evidence.technical_detail: api/ single-app FastAPI service; app/config.py validates PORT within 1..65535; .env.example + .env + .gitignore; GET /health returns {ok:true}.
public_evidence.proof: curl http://localhost:8000/health returned {"ok":true}; PORT=abc/0/70000 produced a clear startup ValidationError; PORT=8000 accepted.
public_evidence.ability: Sets up a runnable service with fail-fast config validation
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the learner can bootstrap a service that fails loudly on misconfiguration instead of breaking silently in production.

terminology_gaps.context: Understood the concept but did not weigh concrete setup/deploy costs numerically.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Invalid PORT values rejected at startup with clear errors before serving traffic.

concepts_demonstrated.concept: environment contract (env var name vs code field)
concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Diagnosed app_port-vs-PORT mismatch from ValidationError and fixed the field name.

teaching_approaches.detail: Showed concrete invalid PORT values and observed the startup errors together
